suspect_claims.claim: Hospice: "6,535 hospices served Medicare beneficiaries in 2023; 1.7 million beneficiaries; $25.7 billion Medicare spend" and bereavement "at most 1.3 ... percentage points" of 2022 margin [MedPAC March 2025]; derived "$334M per year, or about $257 per hospice death".
suspect_claims.problem: STALE by one edition. The file itself cites the March 2026 MedPAC report for home health but used the March 2025 one for hospice. March 2026 Ch. 10 (https://www.medpac.gov/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/Mar26_Ch10_MedPAC_Report_To_Congress_SEC.pdf) reads: "In 2024, 6,706 hospices provided care to Medicare", "1.82 million Medicare beneficiaries received hospice", "expenditures totaled $28.3 billion", and bereavement/volunteer costs would reduce "the aggregate Medicare margin for 2023 by at most 1.1 percentage points and 0.3 percentage points". Re-derived pool is about $311M (1.1% x $28.3B), not $334M. The 1.82M also conflicts with estate.md's 1.91M (Alliance) and the file does not reconcile them; the $257/death figure divides 2023 dollars by a 2024 death count from a different source.

suspect_claims.claim: LifeBio: "over $2 million in revenue with 48 employees", "mostly self-funded with a little angel funding"; "Revenue per employee about $42K ... indicates a labour-heavy service"; presented as the largest sourced dedicated-vendor revenue.
suspect_claims.problem: Quote is verbatim on the Practical Founders page (dated May 5, 2023; page is titled episode #44 although the slug says 43), so not fabricated, but it is a 3.5-year-old podcast host summary and the file missed a material fact: NIH RePORTER (api.reporter.nih.gov, org LIFEBIO INC) lists 7 NIA SBIR awards totalling $5,371,563 for FY2020-FY2026 ($1,384,248 FY2020; $1,556,065 FY2021; $432,337 FY2024; $968,966 FY2025; $1,029,947 FY2026). Grant income of $0.4M-$1.6M a year is a large share of a ~$2M top line, so institutional customer revenue may be well under $2M, 'mostly self-funded' is no longer accurate, and the $42K revenue-per-employee inference is confounded by grant-funded R&D staff. The brief asked for revenue/headcount signals; this one was not found.

suspect_claims.claim: LifeBio: "Starter Story's estimate of about $165K per month in 2023 is a third-party estimator and merely consistent".
suspect_claims.problem: Estimator-only and circular. The fetched Starter Story page says it is compiled by an "AI research system ... from 55 public sources — the founder didn't write it" and shows "Total Revenue ~$2M total as of 2023"; $165K/month is simply $2M/12, i.e. the same podcast number recycled, not corroboration. The file also reports only the estimator that agrees: one search surfaces Growjo at $4M and Prospeo at $6,371,696 (both estimators, both still under $10M). None should be carried in the numbers table as evidence.

suspect_claims.claim: Q8 ceiling: "observed prices of $40-$150 per resident per year: $7.5M-$28.3M" and "To reach $100M at 8.4% penetration needs about $530 per resident per year, three to thirteen times any institutional price found."
suspect_claims.problem: Contradicted by the file's own evidence. The same 2017 article it cites gives MemoryWell at "$450 per article" paid by facilities (530/450 = 1.2x, not 3-13x) and Storii at "$2,500 per year" for "1 to 25 residents" ($100 to $2,500 per resident, not the $80-$154 the file derives by using only the 26-50 tier). $40 is explicitly a floor ("about $2,000 a year to cover less than 50 people"). The headline $8M-$28M cap is therefore built from floor prices on 9-year-old data and the '3 to 13 times' sentence is false as written. Arithmetic itself reproduces (2,256,424 x 8.36% x $40 = $7.5M; x $150 = $28.3M), but the inputs are cherry-picked low; at $450 per resident the same formula gives about $85M.

suspect_claims.claim: All institutional life-story price evidence (LifeBio $2,000 / $5,000-$10,000; Storii $2,500 / $4,000; MemoryWell $450).
suspect_claims.problem: Stale: every figure comes from one trade article dated January 14, 2017 (iadvanceseniorcare.com; quotes verified verbatim). No current institutional price for any life-story vendor was obtained, yet these 2017 prices drive bottom-line points 4 and the ceiling arithmetic without an age caveat in the bottom line.
Overstated. The page says: "In the subsequent 30 years, iN2L has been involved with more than 3,700 senior living communities" -- a cumulative lifetime figure, not a 2022 customer count.

suspect_claims.claim: LifeLoop "trusted by more than 4,700 communities across North America" used as the penetration anchor (8.4%).
suspect_claims.problem: Verified verbatim in the Oct 6, 2026 release, but it is unchanged press-release boilerplate (same 4,700 in January 2026 and May 2026 releases per search), is a vendor self-claim, and has not visibly moved despite the 600 communities added with Linked Senior in 2024 and a lifetime iN2L figure of 3,700. The file treats it as a hard current count and does not note that flat count as evidence for or against growth. LifeLoop's homepage also claims '550K lives' (about 117 per community), which the file did not use and which conflicts with its 83-residents-per-community estimate.

suspect_claims.claim: "assisted-living turnover 71.9% ... A different survey gives 34.5% for 2025 ... either way..."

The 34.5% is a search extract never opened; a factor-of-two disagreement on a load-bearing staffing argument is left unresolved rather than explained (different populations/methods).

suspect_claims.claim: "the top four operate 1,140 communities, 2.7% of assisted-living communities".
suspect_claims.problem: Numerator and denominator are different universes: Argentum counts independent living, memory care and CCRC communities ("independent and assisted living, memory care and continuing care retirement / life plan communities"), the denominator is NCAL assisted living/residential care only. 'Top four' is by units; by community count Sunrise (231) and Atria (170) outrank LCS (119) and Erickson (23). Direction of the conclusion holds; the 2.7% is not a clean statistic.

suspect_claims.claim: "National count of memory-care units from a primary 2026 source: [unknown]" (uses NIC/broker search extracts: 247,200; 255,000-270,000; 5,750 properties).
suspect_claims.problem: The file's own primary source (NCAL Fast Facts, June 2026) states "18% have a designated unit/wing/floor" and "11% only serve adults with dementia", which gives a national community-level memory-care count (about 29% of 41,465, roughly 12,000 communities). It was not used; the answer instead rests on unread search extracts.

suspect_claims.claim: "LifeBio's $40 per resident per year sits inside that" ($9-$23 per resident per month activities budget).
suspect_claims.problem: Unit mismatch: $40 a year is $3.33 a month, which is below, not inside, a $9-$23 monthly range. The underlying budget figures are undated forum posts never fetched (site was down).
